title: Trace: Definition and the Cyclic Law
quickIdea: The trace is the sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix; it is linear, it survives transposition, and it obeys the cyclic law tr(AB) = tr(BA) even for rectangular factors.
remember: tr(A) is the sum a_11 + a_22 + ... + a_nn, defined for square matrices only.
tr(A + B) = tr(A) + tr(B), tr(kA) = k tr(A), tr(A^T) = tr(A).
tr(AB) = tr(BA) whenever both products exist, even when A is m x n and B is n x m, so the two traces come from matrices of different orders.
Only cyclic shifts are allowed: tr(ABC) = tr(CAB) = tr(BCA), but tr(ABC) and tr(ACB) can differ.
tr(A) equals the sum of the eigenvalues of A, counted with multiplicity, which is why tr(A^k) is the sum of the k-th powers of the eigenvalues.

example.prompt: A = [[1,2],[3,4]] and B = [[0,1],[1,0]]. Compare tr(AB), tr(BA) and tr(A) tr(B).
example.answer: tr(AB) = tr(BA) = 5, while tr(A) tr(B) = 0: the trace of a product is not the product of the traces.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2022 Q.10 asks whether tr(AB) = tr(BA) still holds for rectangular A and B; both of its statements are true, and the reason is the double-sum identity rather than eigenvalues.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A is 2 x 3, B is 3 x 2 and tr(AB) = 7. What is tr(BA)?
variations.why: The cyclic law holds for any conformable pair, so the trace of the 2 x 2 product equals the trace of the 3 x 3 product.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why is tr(AB) = tr(BA) true when A and B are not square?
variations.answer: tr(AB) is the sum over i and k of a_ik b_ki, and tr(BA) is the sum over k and i of b_ki a_ik; the same products are added in a different order.
variations.why: A finite sum of scalars does not depend on the order of summation, and no other term appears in either sum.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A is 3 x 3 with eigenvalues 1, 2 and 3. What is tr(A^2)?
variations.why: The eigenvalues of A^2 are the squares 1, 4 and 9, and the trace of A^2 is their sum.

trap.what: Assuming the trace survives any reordering of three factors, so that tr(ABC) = tr(ACB).
trap.why: The trace law only permits cyclic shifts; swapping two factors changes the product itself.

check.question: A is 4 x 4 with tr(A) = 3. What is tr(2A^T)?
check.explanation: tr(2A^T) = 2 tr(A^T) = 2 tr(A) = 6, using linearity and then the transpose law.
